Let me analyze these teaching examples carefully to identify systematic errors in the forecasts compared to true outcomes.

Looking at the examples, I need to identify patterns in the differences between model forecasts and true outcomes.

## Example 1 (2024-09-04)
History: Prices have been generally declining from peak 73.14 down to 68.16 over 18 days
Model forecasts: Start at 67.58 and gradually increase to 72.38
True outcomes: Start at 67.00 and gradually decline to 61.76

The model is forecasting prices that are too HIGH compared to the true declining trajectory.

## Example 2 (2024-08-23)
History: Similar pattern - prices declining from 73.14 to 67.00
Model forecasts: Start at 71.40, gradually increasing to 70.91
True outcomes: Start at 71.13, gradually declining to 62.76

Again, model forecasts are approximately 1-2 points too high initially, and the decline is underestimated.

## Example 3 (2024-08-26)
Very similar to Example 2 - model forecasts are slightly above true outcomes.

## Example 4 (2024-08-22)
Model forecasts start at 71.84 vs true 71.57 ( +0.27)
By day 10, model is at 71.35 vs true 66.35 ( +5 points!)

## Example 5 (2024-08-27)
Model forecasts start at 71.82 vs true 71.49 ( +0.33)
By day 10, model is at 70.77 vs true 65.77 ( +5 points!)

Let me look more closely at the pattern:

Looking at Example 1 in more detail:
- Day 0: Model 67.58 vs True 67.00 (error +0.58)


- Day 1: Model 67.31 vs True 66.20 (error +1.11)
- Day 2: Model 68.06 vs True 66.50 (error +1.56)
- Day 3: Model 68.37 vs True 66.52 (error +1.85)
- Day 4: Model 66.90 vs True 64.92 (error +1.98)
- Day 5: Model 68.42 vs True 66.40 (error +2.02)

I notice a consistent pattern
